-- | Avro serialization support for Haskell
--   
--   Avro serialization and deserialization support for Haskell
@package avro
@version 0.6.2.1

module Data.Avro.Codec

-- | A <a>Codec</a> allows for compression/decompression of a block in an
--   Avro container according to the Avro spec.
data Codec
Codec :: ByteString -> (forall a. () => Decompress a) -> (ByteString -> ByteString) -> Codec

-- | The name of the codec according to the Avro spec.
[codecName] :: Codec -> ByteString

-- | Execute a <a>Get</a> over a chunk of bytes possibly decompressing the
--   chunk incrementally.
--   
--   The API is somewhat more complex than say <a>codecCompress</a> to
--   allow interleaving of decompression and binary decoding while still
--   allowing proper error handling without resorting to async exceptions.
[codecDecompress] :: Codec -> forall a. () => Decompress a

-- | Compresses a lazy stream of bytes.
[codecCompress] :: Codec -> ByteString -> ByteString

-- | Block decompression function for blocks of Avro.
type Decompress a = ByteString -> Get a -> Either String a

-- | <a>nullCodec</a> specifies <tt>null</tt> required by Avro spec. (see
--   <a>https://avro.apache.org/docs/1.8.1/spec.html#null</a>)
nullCodec :: Codec

-- | <a>deflateCodec</a> specifies <tt>deflate</tt> codec required by Avro
--   spec. (see
--   <a>https://avro.apache.org/docs/1.8.1/spec.html#deflate</a>)
deflateCodec :: Codec

-- | An internal module that contains common decoding functionality that is
--   shared between Lazy and Strict decoders, as well as generic <a>Get</a>
--   monad helpers.
module Data.Avro.Internal.Get
getBoolean :: Get Bool

-- | Get a 32-bit int (zigzag encoded, max of 5 bytes)
getInt :: Get Int32

-- | Get a 64 bit int (zigzag encoded, max of 10 bytes)
getLong :: Get Int64

-- | Get an zigzag encoded integral value consuming bytes till the msb is
--   0.
getZigZag :: (Bits i, Integral i, DecodeRaw i) => Get i
getBytes :: Get ByteString
getBytesLazy :: Get ByteString
getString :: Get Text
getFloat :: Get Float
getDouble :: Get Double

-- | Avro encodes arrays and maps as a series of blocks. Each block starts
--   with a count of the elements in the block. A series of blocks is
--   always terminated with an empty block (encoded as a 0).
decodeBlocks :: Get a -> Get [a]
sFromIntegral :: forall a b m. (Monad m, Bounded a, Bounded b, Integral a, Integral b) => a -> m b

module Data.Avro.Schema.Decimal
data Decimal (p :: Nat) (s :: Nat)
fromUnderlyingValue :: forall (p :: Nat) (s :: Nat). KnownNat s => Integer -> Decimal p s
underlyingValue :: forall (s :: Nat) (p :: Nat). (KnownNat p, KnownNat s) => Decimal p s -> Maybe Int
instance GHC.Classes.Eq (Data.Avro.Schema.Decimal.Decimal p s)

-- | Avro <a>Schema</a>s, represented here as values of type <a>Schema</a>,
--   describe the serialization and de-serialization of values.
--   
--   In Avro schemas are compose-able such that encoding data under a
--   schema and decoding with a variant, such as newer or older version of
--   the original schema, can be accomplished by using the
--   <a>Deconflict</a> module.
module Data.Avro.Schema.Schema

-- | N.B. It is possible to create a Haskell value (of <a>Schema</a> type)
--   that is not a valid Avro schema by violating one of the above or one
--   of the conditions called out in <a>validateSchema</a>.
data Schema
Null :: Schema
Boolean :: Schema
Int :: Maybe LogicalTypeInt -> Schema
[logicalTypeI] :: Schema -> Maybe LogicalTypeInt
Long :: Maybe LogicalTypeLong -> Schema
[logicalTypeL] :: Schema -> Maybe LogicalTypeLong
Float :: Schema
Double :: Schema
Bytes :: Maybe LogicalTypeBytes -> Schema
[logicalTypeB] :: Schema -> Maybe LogicalTypeBytes
String :: Maybe LogicalTypeString -> Schema
[logicalTypeS] :: Schema -> Maybe LogicalTypeString
Array :: Schema -> Schema
[item] :: Schema -> Schema
Map :: Schema -> Schema
[values] :: Schema -> Schema
NamedType :: TypeName -> Schema
Record :: TypeName -> [TypeName] -> Maybe Text -> [Field] -> Schema
[name] :: Schema -> TypeName
[aliases] :: Schema -> [TypeName]
[doc] :: Schema -> Maybe Text
[fields] :: Schema -> [Field]
Enum :: TypeName -> [TypeName] -> Maybe Text -> Vector Text -> Schema
[name] :: Schema -> TypeName
[aliases] :: Schema -> [TypeName]
[doc] :: Schema -> Maybe Text
[symbols] :: Schema -> Vector Text
Union :: Vector Schema -> Schema
[options] :: Schema -> Vector Schema
Fixed :: TypeName -> [TypeName] -> Int -> Maybe LogicalTypeFixed -> Schema
[name] :: Schema -> TypeName
[aliases] :: Schema -> [TypeName]
[size] :: Schema -> Int
[logicalTypeF] :: Schema -> Maybe LogicalTypeFixed
pattern Int' :: Schema
pattern Long' :: Schema
pattern Bytes' :: Schema
pattern String' :: Schema
data DefaultValue
DNull :: DefaultValue
DBoolean :: !Bool -> DefaultValue
DInt :: Schema -> {-# UNPACK #-}Int32 -> DefaultValue
DLong :: Schema -> {-# UNPACK #-}Int64 -> DefaultValue
DFloat :: Schema -> {-# UNPACK #-}Float -> DefaultValue
DDouble :: Schema -> {-# UNPACK #-}Double -> DefaultValue
DBytes :: Schema -> {-# UNPACK #-}ByteString -> DefaultValue
DString :: Schema -> {-# UNPACK #-}Text -> DefaultValue

-- | Dynamically enforced monomorphic type.
DArray :: Vector DefaultValue -> DefaultValue

-- | Dynamically enforced monomorphic type
DMap :: HashMap Text DefaultValue -> DefaultValue
DRecord :: Schema -> HashMap Text DefaultValue -> DefaultValue

-- | Set of union options, schema for selected option, and the actual
--   value.
DUnion :: Vector Schema -> Schema -> DefaultValue -> DefaultValue
DFixed :: Schema -> {-# UNPACK #-} !ByteString -> DefaultValue

-- | An enum is a set of the possible symbols (the schema) and the selected
--   symbol
DEnum :: Schema -> {-# UNPACK #-}Int -> Text -> DefaultValue
data Field
Field :: Text -> [Text] -> Maybe Text -> Maybe Order -> Schema -> Maybe DefaultValue -> Field
[fldName] :: Field -> Text
[fldAliases] :: Field -> [Text]
[fldDoc] :: Field -> Maybe Text
[fldOrder] :: Field -> Maybe Order
[fldType] :: Field -> Schema
[fldDefault] :: Field -> Maybe DefaultValue
data Order
Ascending :: Order
Descending :: Order
Ignore :: Order

-- | A named type in Avro has a name and, optionally, a namespace.
--   
--   A name is a string that starts with an ASCII letter or underscore
--   followed by letters, underscores and digits:
--   
--   <pre>
--   name ::= [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*
--   </pre>
--   
--   Examples include <tt>"_foo7"</tt>, <tt><a>Bar_</a></tt> and
--   <tt>"x"</tt>.
--   
--   A namespace is a sequence of names with the same lexical structure.
--   When written as a string, the components of a namespace are separated
--   with dots (<tt>"com.example"</tt>).
--   
--   <a>TypeName</a> represents a <i>fullname</i>—a name combined with a
--   namespace. These are written and parsed as dot-separated strings. The
--   <a>TypeName</a> <tt>TN <a>Foo</a> ["com", "example"]</tt> is rendered
--   as <tt>"com.example.Foo"</tt>.
--   
--   Fullnames have to be globally unique inside an Avro schema.
--   
--   A namespace of <tt>[]</tt> or <tt>[""]</tt> is the "null namespace".
--   In avro an explicitly null-namespaced identifier is written as ".Foo"
data TypeName
TN :: Text -> [Text] -> TypeName
[baseName] :: TypeName -> Text
[namespace] :: TypeName -> [Text]

-- | The <tt>decimal</tt> logical type represents arbitrary-precision
--   decimal numbers. Numbers are represented as <tt>unscaled * (10 **
--   -scale)</tt> where <tt>scale</tt> is part of the logical type and
--   <tt>unscaled</tt> is an integer represented by the underlying
--   primitive type.
--   
--   Instances of the <tt>decimal</tt> logical type need to specify a
--   <tt>scale</tt> and <tt>precision</tt>.
--   
--   <tt>decimal</tt> can be encoded as one of several different primitive
--   types:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li><pre>bytes</pre></li>
--   <li><pre>fixed</pre></li>
--   <li><pre>long</pre></li>
--   <li><pre>int</pre></li>
--   </ul>
--   
--   For <tt>long</tt> and <tt>int</tt>, <tt>unscaled</tt> is the
--   underlying number.
--   
--   For <tt>bytes</tt> and <tt>fixed</tt>, <tt>unscaled</tt> is
--   represented as a two's-complement signed integer in big-endian byte
--   order.
--   
--   Note: <tt>int</tt> and <tt>long</tt> representations for
--   <tt>decimal</tt> are not part of the <a>current Avro
--   specification</a>, but they are supported by some language
--   implementations including the official Java library. Implementations
--   that do not support this should ignore the logical type and use the
--   underlying primitive type instead.
data Decimal
Decimal :: Integer -> Integer -> Decimal

-- | The maximum number of digits that can be represented by this
--   <tt>decimal</tt> type.
--   
--   <pre>
--   precision &gt; 0
--   </pre>
[precision] :: Decimal -> Integer

-- | The <tt>scale</tt> in <tt>unscaled * (10 ** -scale)</tt> for this
--   type.
--   
--   <pre>
--   0 ≤ scale ≤ precision
--   </pre>
[scale] :: Decimal -> Integer
newtype LogicalTypeBytes

-- | An arbitrary-precision signed decimal number. See <a>Decimal</a>.
DecimalB :: Decimal -> LogicalTypeBytes
data LogicalTypeFixed

-- | An arbitrary-precision signed decimal number. See <a>Decimal</a>.
DecimalF :: Decimal -> LogicalTypeFixed

-- | An interval of time, represented as some number of months, days and
--   milliseconds.
--   
--   Encoded as three little-endian unsigned integers for months, days and
--   milliseconds respectively.
Duration :: LogicalTypeFixed
data LogicalTypeInt

-- | An arbitrary-precision signed decimal number. See <a>Decimal</a>.
DecimalI :: Decimal -> LogicalTypeInt

-- | A date (eg <tt>2020-01-10</tt>) with no timezone/locale.
--   
--   Encoded as the number of days before/after the Unix epoch
--   (1970-01-01).
Date :: LogicalTypeInt

-- | A time of day with millisecond precision.
--   
--   Encoded as the number of milliseconds after midnight.
TimeMillis :: LogicalTypeInt
data LogicalTypeLong

-- | An arbitrary-precision signed decimal number. See <a>Decimal</a>.
DecimalL :: Decimal -> LogicalTypeLong

-- | A time of day with microsecond precision.
--   
--   Encoded as the number of microseconds after midnight.
TimeMicros :: LogicalTypeLong

-- | A UTC timestamp with millisecond precision.
--   
--   Encoded as the number of milliseconds before/after the Unix epoch
--   (1970-01-01 00:00:00.000).
TimestampMillis :: LogicalTypeLong

-- | A UTC timestamp with microsecond precision.
--   
--   Encoded as the number of microseconds before/after the Unix epoch
--   (1970-01-01 00:00:00.000000).
TimestampMicros :: LogicalTypeLong

-- | A timestamp in the local timezone, whatever that happens to be, with
--   millisecond precision.
--   
--   Encoded as the number of milliseconds before/after the Unix epoch
--   (1970-01-01 00:00:00.000).
LocalTimestampMillis :: LogicalTypeLong

-- | A timestamp in the local timezone, whatever that happens to be, with
--   microsecond precision.
--   
--   Encoded as the number of microseconds before/after the Unix epoch
--   (1970-01-01 00:00:00.000000).
LocalTimestampMicros :: LogicalTypeLong
data LogicalTypeString

-- | A Universally Unique Identifier (UUID).
--   
--   Encoded as a string that is valid according to <a>RFC 4122</a>.
UUID :: LogicalTypeString

-- | Render a fullname as a dot separated string.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt; renderFullname (TN <a>Foo</a> ["com", "example"])
--   "com.example.Foo"
--   </pre>
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt; renderFullname (TN <a>Foo</a> [])
--   ".Foo"
--   </pre>
renderFullname :: TypeName -> Text

-- | Parses a fullname into a <a>TypeName</a>, assuming the string
--   representation is valid.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt; parseFullname "com.example.Foo"
--   TN { baseName = <a>Foo</a>, components = ["com", "example"] }
--   </pre>
parseFullname :: Text -> TypeName

-- | Build an <a>Enum</a> value from its components.
mkEnum :: TypeName -> [TypeName] -> Maybe Text -> [Text] -> Schema

-- | <tt>mkUnion subTypes</tt> Defines a union of the provided subTypes.
--   N.B. it is invalid Avro to include another union or to have more than
--   one of the same type as a direct member of the union. No check is done
--   for this condition!
mkUnion :: NonEmpty Schema -> Schema

-- | Placeholder NO-OP function!
--   
--   Validates a schema to ensure:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li>All types are defined</li>
--   <li>Unions do not directly contain other unions</li>
--   <li>Unions are not ambiguous (may not contain more than one schema
--   with the same type except for named types of record, fixed and
--   enum)</li>
--   <li>Default values for unions can be cast as the type indicated by the
--   first structure.</li>
--   <li>Default values can be cast/de-serialize correctly.</li>
--   <li>Named types are resolvable</li>
--   </ul>
validateSchema :: Schema -> Parser ()

-- | Get the name of the type. In the case of unions, get the name of the
--   first value in the union schema.
typeName :: Schema -> Text

-- | Get the aliases of the type.
typeAliases :: Schema -> [TypeName]

-- | <tt>buildTypeEnvironment schema</tt> builds a function mapping type
--   names to the types declared in the traversed schema.
--   
--   This mapping includes both the base type names and any aliases they
--   have. Aliases and normal names are not differentiated in any way.
buildTypeEnvironment :: Applicative m => (TypeName -> m Schema) -> Schema -> TypeName -> m Schema

-- | <tt>extractBindings schema</tt> traverses a schema and builds a map of
--   all declared types.
--   
--   Types declared implicitly in record field definitions are also
--   included. No distinction is made between aliases and normal names.
extractBindings :: Schema -> HashMap TypeName Schema
data Result a
Success :: a -> Result a
Error :: String -> Result a
badValue :: Show t => t -> String -> Result a
resultToEither :: Result b -> Either String b

-- | Checks that two schemas match. This is like equality of schemas,
--   except <tt>NamedTypes</tt> match against other types <i>with the same
--   name</i>.
--   
--   This extends recursively: two records match if they have the same
--   name, the same number of fields and the fields all match.
matches :: Schema -> Schema -> Bool

-- | Parses a string literal into a bytestring in the format expected for
--   bytes and fixed values. Will fail if every character does not have a
--   codepoint between 0 and 255.
parseBytes :: Text -> Result ByteString

-- | Turn a <tt>ByteString</tt> into a <a>Text</a> that matches the format
--   Avro expects from bytes and fixed literals in JSON. Each byte is
--   mapped to a single Unicode codepoint between 0 and 255.
serializeBytes :: ByteString -> Text

-- | Parse JSON-encoded avro data.
parseAvroJSON :: (Schema -> Value -> Result DefaultValue) -> (TypeName -> Maybe Schema) -> Schema -> Value -> Result DefaultValue

-- | Merge two schemas to produce a third. Specifically, <tt>overlay schema
--   reference</tt> fills in <tt>NamedTypes</tt> in <tt>schema</tt> using
--   any matching definitions from <tt>reference</tt>.
overlay :: Schema -> Schema -> Schema

-- | Extract the named inner type definition as its own schema.
subdefinition :: Schema -> Text -> Maybe Schema
expandNamedTypes :: Schema -> Schema
instance GHC.Internal.Base.Alternative Data.Avro.Schema.Schema.Result

module Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema

-- | This type represents a <i>deconflicted</i> version of a
--   <tt>Schema</tt>. Schema resolution is described in Avro specification:
--   <a>https://avro.apache.org/docs/current/spec.html#Schema+Resolution</a>
--   
--   This library represents "normal" schema and "deconflicted" schema as
--   different types to avoid confusion between these two usecases (we
--   shouldn't serialise values with such schema) and to be able to
--   accomodate some extra information that links between how data is
--   supposed transformed between what reader wants and what writer has.
data ReadSchema
Null :: ReadSchema
Boolean :: ReadSchema
Int :: Maybe LogicalTypeInt -> ReadSchema
[logicalTypeI] :: ReadSchema -> Maybe LogicalTypeInt
Long :: ReadLong -> Maybe LogicalTypeLong -> ReadSchema
[longReadFrom] :: ReadSchema -> ReadLong
[logicalTypeL] :: ReadSchema -> Maybe LogicalTypeLong
Float :: ReadFloat -> ReadSchema
[floatReadFrom] :: ReadSchema -> ReadFloat
Double :: ReadDouble -> ReadSchema
[doubleReadFrom] :: ReadSchema -> ReadDouble
Bytes :: Maybe LogicalTypeBytes -> ReadSchema
[logicalTypeB] :: ReadSchema -> Maybe LogicalTypeBytes
String :: Maybe LogicalTypeString -> ReadSchema
[logicalTypeS] :: ReadSchema -> Maybe LogicalTypeString
Array :: ReadSchema -> ReadSchema
[item] :: ReadSchema -> ReadSchema
Map :: ReadSchema -> ReadSchema
[values] :: ReadSchema -> ReadSchema
NamedType :: TypeName -> ReadSchema
Record :: TypeName -> [TypeName] -> Maybe Text -> [ReadField] -> ReadSchema
[name] :: ReadSchema -> TypeName
[aliases] :: ReadSchema -> [TypeName]
[doc] :: ReadSchema -> Maybe Text
[fields] :: ReadSchema -> [ReadField]
Enum :: TypeName -> [TypeName] -> Maybe Text -> Vector Text -> ReadSchema
[name] :: ReadSchema -> TypeName
[aliases] :: ReadSchema -> [TypeName]
[doc] :: ReadSchema -> Maybe Text
[symbols] :: ReadSchema -> Vector Text
Union :: Vector (Int, ReadSchema) -> ReadSchema

-- | Order of values represents order in the writer schema, an index
--   represents order in a reader schema
[options] :: ReadSchema -> Vector (Int, ReadSchema)
Fixed :: TypeName -> [TypeName] -> Int -> Maybe LogicalTypeFixed -> ReadSchema
[name] :: ReadSchema -> TypeName
[aliases] :: ReadSchema -> [TypeName]
[size] :: ReadSchema -> Int
[logicalTypeF] :: ReadSchema -> Maybe LogicalTypeFixed
FreeUnion :: Int -> ReadSchema -> ReadSchema
[pos] :: ReadSchema -> Int
[ty] :: ReadSchema -> ReadSchema

-- | Deconflicted record field.
data ReadField
ReadField :: Text -> [Text] -> Maybe Text -> Maybe Order -> FieldStatus -> ReadSchema -> Maybe DefaultValue -> ReadField
[fldName] :: ReadField -> Text
[fldAliases] :: ReadField -> [Text]
[fldDoc] :: ReadField -> Maybe Text
[fldOrder] :: ReadField -> Maybe Order

-- | How the value of this field should be treated. See <a>FieldStatus</a>
--   documentation.
[fldStatus] :: ReadField -> FieldStatus
[fldType] :: ReadField -> ReadSchema
[fldDefault] :: ReadField -> Maybe DefaultValue

-- | How to decode a value of target type <tt>Long</tt>. This type controls
--   how many bits are needed to be read from the encoded bytestring. The
--   number of bits can be different depending on differences between
--   reader and writer schemas.
--   
--   The rules are described in
--   <a>https://avro.apache.org/docs/current/spec.html#Schema+Resolution</a>
data ReadLong

-- | Read <tt>Int</tt> (32 bits) and cast it to <tt>Long</tt> (Rule: int is
--   promotable to long, float, or double)
LongFromInt :: ReadLong

-- | Read <tt>Long</tt> (64 bits) and use as is
ReadLong :: ReadLong

-- | How to decode a value of target type <tt>Float</tt>. This type
--   controls how many bits are needed to be read from the encoded
--   bytestring. The number of bits can be different depending on
--   differences between reader and writer schemas.
--   
--   The rules are described in
--   <a>https://avro.apache.org/docs/current/spec.html#Schema+Resolution</a>
data ReadFloat

-- | Read <tt>Int</tt> (32 bits) and cast it to <tt>Float</tt>
FloatFromInt :: ReadFloat

-- | Read <tt>Long</tt> (64 bits) and cast it to <tt>Float</tt> (Rule: long
--   is promotable to float or double)
FloatFromLong :: ReadFloat

-- | Read <tt>Float</tt> and use as is
ReadFloat :: ReadFloat

-- | How to decode a value of target type <tt>Double</tt>. This type
--   controls how many bits are needed to be read from the encoded
--   bytestring. The number of bits can be different depending on
--   differences between reader and writer schemas.
--   
--   The rules are described in
--   <a>https://avro.apache.org/docs/current/spec.html#Schema+Resolution</a>
data ReadDouble

-- | Read <tt>Int</tt> (32 bits) and cast it to <tt>Double</tt> (Rule: int
--   is promotable to long, float, or double)
DoubleFromInt :: ReadDouble

-- | Read <tt>Float</tt> (64 bits) and cast it to <tt>Double</tt> (Rule:
--   float is promotable to float or double)
DoubleFromFloat :: ReadDouble

-- | Read <tt>Long</tt> (64 bits) and cast it to <tt>Double</tt> (Rule:
--   long is promotable to float or double)
DoubleFromLong :: ReadDouble
ReadDouble :: ReadDouble

-- | Converts Avro Schema to ReaderSchema trivially. This function is
--   useful when no deconflicting is required.
fromSchema :: Schema -> ReadSchema
fromField :: FieldStatus -> Field -> ReadField

-- | <tt>extractBindings schema</tt> traverses a schema and builds a map of
--   all declared types.
--   
--   Types declared implicitly in record field definitions are also
--   included. No distinction is made between aliases and normal names.
extractBindings :: ReadSchema -> HashMap TypeName ReadSchema

-- | The <tt>decimal</tt> logical type represents arbitrary-precision
--   decimal numbers. Numbers are represented as <tt>unscaled * (10 **
--   -scale)</tt> where <tt>scale</tt> is part of the logical type and
--   <tt>unscaled</tt> is an integer represented by the underlying
--   primitive type.
--   
--   Instances of the <tt>decimal</tt> logical type need to specify a
--   <tt>scale</tt> and <tt>precision</tt>.
--   
--   <tt>decimal</tt> can be encoded as one of several different primitive
--   types:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li><pre>bytes</pre></li>
--   <li><pre>fixed</pre></li>
--   <li><pre>long</pre></li>
--   <li><pre>int</pre></li>
--   </ul>
--   
--   For <tt>long</tt> and <tt>int</tt>, <tt>unscaled</tt> is the
--   underlying number.
--   
--   For <tt>bytes</tt> and <tt>fixed</tt>, <tt>unscaled</tt> is
--   represented as a two's-complement signed integer in big-endian byte
--   order.
--   
--   Note: <tt>int</tt> and <tt>long</tt> representations for
--   <tt>decimal</tt> are not part of the <a>current Avro
--   specification</a>, but they are supported by some language
--   implementations including the official Java library. Implementations
--   that do not support this should ignore the logical type and use the
--   underlying primitive type instead.
data Decimal
Decimal :: Integer -> Integer -> Decimal

-- | The maximum number of digits that can be represented by this
--   <tt>decimal</tt> type.
--   
--   <pre>
--   precision &gt; 0
--   </pre>
[precision] :: Decimal -> Integer

-- | The <tt>scale</tt> in <tt>unscaled * (10 ** -scale)</tt> for this
--   type.
--   
--   <pre>
--   0 ≤ scale ≤ precision
--   </pre>
[scale] :: Decimal -> Integer
newtype LogicalTypeBytes

-- | An arbitrary-precision signed decimal number. See <a>Decimal</a>.
DecimalB :: Decimal -> LogicalTypeBytes
data LogicalTypeFixed

-- | An arbitrary-precision signed decimal number. See <a>Decimal</a>.
DecimalF :: Decimal -> LogicalTypeFixed

-- | An interval of time, represented as some number of months, days and
--   milliseconds.
--   
--   Encoded as three little-endian unsigned integers for months, days and
--   milliseconds respectively.
Duration :: LogicalTypeFixed
data LogicalTypeInt

-- | An arbitrary-precision signed decimal number. See <a>Decimal</a>.
DecimalI :: Decimal -> LogicalTypeInt

-- | A date (eg <tt>2020-01-10</tt>) with no timezone/locale.
--   
--   Encoded as the number of days before/after the Unix epoch
--   (1970-01-01).
Date :: LogicalTypeInt

-- | A time of day with millisecond precision.
--   
--   Encoded as the number of milliseconds after midnight.
TimeMillis :: LogicalTypeInt
data LogicalTypeLong

-- | An arbitrary-precision signed decimal number. See <a>Decimal</a>.
DecimalL :: Decimal -> LogicalTypeLong

-- | A time of day with microsecond precision.
--   
--   Encoded as the number of microseconds after midnight.
TimeMicros :: LogicalTypeLong

-- | A UTC timestamp with millisecond precision.
--   
--   Encoded as the number of milliseconds before/after the Unix epoch
--   (1970-01-01 00:00:00.000).
TimestampMillis :: LogicalTypeLong

-- | A UTC timestamp with microsecond precision.
--   
--   Encoded as the number of microseconds before/after the Unix epoch
--   (1970-01-01 00:00:00.000000).
TimestampMicros :: LogicalTypeLong

-- | A timestamp in the local timezone, whatever that happens to be, with
--   millisecond precision.
--   
--   Encoded as the number of milliseconds before/after the Unix epoch
--   (1970-01-01 00:00:00.000).
LocalTimestampMillis :: LogicalTypeLong

-- | A timestamp in the local timezone, whatever that happens to be, with
--   microsecond precision.
--   
--   Encoded as the number of microseconds before/after the Unix epoch
--   (1970-01-01 00:00:00.000000).
LocalTimestampMicros :: LogicalTypeLong
data LogicalTypeString

-- | A Universally Unique Identifier (UUID).
--   
--   Encoded as a string that is valid according to <a>RFC 4122</a>.
UUID :: LogicalTypeString

-- | Depending on differences between reader and writer schemas, a record
--   field can be found:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li>Present in the reader schema but missing from the writer schema.
--   In this case the reader field is marked as <a>Defaulted</a> with the
--   default value from the reader schema. An index value represents the
--   position of the field in the reader schema.</li>
--   <li>Present in the writer schema but missing from the reader schema.
--   In this case the record field is marked as <a>Ignored</a>: the
--   corresponding bytes still need to be read from the payload (to advance
--   the position in a bytestring), but the result is discarded.</li>
--   <li>Present in both reader and writer schemas. In this case the field
--   is marked to be read <a>AsIs</a> with an index that represents the
--   field's position in the reader schema.</li>
--   </ul>
data FieldStatus
AsIs :: Int -> FieldStatus
Ignored :: FieldStatus
Defaulted :: Int -> DefaultValue -> FieldStatus
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.FieldStatus
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.ReadDouble
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.ReadField
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.ReadFloat
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.ReadLong
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.ReadSchema
instance GHC.Internal.Generics.Generic Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.FieldStatus
instance GHC.Internal.Generics.Generic Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.ReadDouble
instance GHC.Internal.Generics.Generic Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.ReadField
instance GHC.Internal.Generics.Generic Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.ReadFloat
instance GHC.Internal.Generics.Generic Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.ReadLong
instance GHC.Internal.Generics.Generic Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.ReadSchema
instance Control.DeepSeq.NFData Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.FieldStatus
instance Control.DeepSeq.NFData Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.ReadDouble
instance Control.DeepSeq.NFData Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.ReadField
instance Control.DeepSeq.NFData Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.ReadFloat
instance Control.DeepSeq.NFData Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.ReadLong
instance Control.DeepSeq.NFData Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.ReadSchema
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.FieldStatus
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.ReadDouble
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.ReadFloat
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.ReadLong
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.FieldStatus
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.ReadDouble
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.ReadField
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.ReadFloat
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.ReadLong
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Data.Avro.Schema.ReadSchema.ReadSchema

module Data.Avro.Schema.Deconflict

-- | <tt>deconflict writer reader</tt> will produce a schema that can
--   decode with the writer's schema into the form specified by the
--   reader's schema.
--   
--   Schema resolution rules are described by the specification:
--   <a>https://avro.apache.org/docs/current/spec.html#Schema+Resolution</a>
deconflict :: Schema -> Schema -> Either String ReadSchema

-- | Avro supports a JSON representation of Avro objects alongside the Avro
--   binary format. An Avro schema can be used to generate and validate
--   JSON representations of Avro objects.
--   
--   The JSON format is the same format as used for default values in
--   schemas except unions are encoded differently. Non-union values are
--   encoded as follows:
--   
--   TODO: table
--   
--   (Table from the Avro 1.8.2 specification:
--   <a>https://avro.apache.org/docs/1.8.2/spec.html#schema_record</a>)
--   
--   Bytes and fixed are encoded as JSON strings where each byte is
--   translated into the corresponding Unicode codepoint between 0–255,
--   which includes non-printable characters. Note that this encoding
--   happens at the Unicode code-point level, meaning it is independent of
--   text encoding. (JSON is, by definition, encoded in UTF8.)
--   
--   Unions are encoded as an object with a single field that specifies the
--   "branch" of the union. If the branch is a primitive type like
--   <tt>"string"</tt>, the name of the primitive type is used:
--   
--   <pre>
--   { "string" : "foo" }
--   </pre>
--   
--   For named types (record, enum and fixed), the name of the type is
--   used:
--   
--   <pre>
--   { <a>MyRecord</a> : { ... } }
--   </pre>
module Data.Avro.JSON
decodeAvroJSON :: Schema -> Value -> Result DefaultValue

module Data.Avro.Encoding.ToAvro
newtype Encoder
Encoder :: (Schema -> Builder) -> Encoder
[runEncoder] :: Encoder -> Schema -> Builder
(.=) :: ToAvro a => Text -> a -> (Text, Encoder)
record :: Schema -> [(Text, Encoder)] -> Builder

-- | Describes how to encode Haskell data types into Avro bytes
class ToAvro a
toAvro :: ToAvro a => Schema -> a -> Builder
instance (GHC.Internal.Ix.Ix i, Data.Avro.Encoding.ToAvro.ToAvro a) => Data.Avro.Encoding.ToAvro.ToAvro (GHC.Internal.Arr.Array i a)

module Data.Avro.Internal.Container
data ContainerHeader
ContainerHeader :: ByteString -> (forall a. () => Decompress a) -> Schema -> ContainerHeader
[syncBytes] :: ContainerHeader -> ByteString
[decompress] :: ContainerHeader -> forall a. () => Decompress a
[containedSchema] :: ContainerHeader -> Schema
nrSyncBytes :: Integral sb => sb

-- | Generates a new synchronization marker for encoding Avro containers
newSyncBytes :: IO ByteString
getContainerHeader :: Get ContainerHeader

-- | Reads the container as a list of blocks without decoding them into
--   actual values.
--   
--   This can be useful for streaming <i> splitting </i> merging Avro
--   containers without paying the cost for Avro encoding/decoding.
--   
--   Each block is returned as a raw <a>ByteString</a> annotated with the
--   number of Avro values that are contained in this block.
--   
--   The "outer" error represents the error in opening the container itself
--   (including problems like reading schemas embedded into the container.)
decodeRawBlocks :: ByteString -> Either String (Schema, [Either String (Int, ByteString)])
data Blocks a
Block :: a -> Blocks a -> Blocks a

-- | Feed more bytes. Pass the empty ByteString to signal end of input.
More :: (ByteString -> Blocks a) -> Blocks a
Error :: String -> ByteString -> Blocks a

-- | Leftover bytes
Done :: ByteString -> Blocks a

-- | Feeds a <a>ByteString</a> to the <a>Blocks</a> until exhausted.
--   Consumes the <a>ByteString</a> lazily.
foldrBlocks :: (a -> b -> b) -> (String -> b) -> b -> ByteString -> Blocks a -> b
decodeRawBlocksIncremental :: ContainerHeader -> Blocks (Int, ByteString)

-- | Splits container into a list of individual avro-encoded values. This
--   version provides both encoded and decoded values.
--   
--   This is particularly useful when slicing up containers into one or
--   more smaller files. By extracting the original bytestring it is
--   possible to avoid re-encoding data.
extractContainerValuesBytes :: forall a schema. (Schema -> Either String schema) -> (schema -> Get a) -> ByteString -> Either String (Schema, [Either String (a, ByteString)])
extractContainerValues :: forall a schema. (Schema -> Either String schema) -> (schema -> Get a) -> ByteString -> Either String (Schema, [Either String a])
extractContainerValuesIncremental :: (Schema -> Either String schema) -> (schema -> Get a) -> ContainerHeader -> Either String (Schema, Blocks [Either String a])

-- | Packs a container from a given list of already encoded Avro values
--   Each bytestring should represent exactly one one value serialised to
--   Avro.
packContainerValues :: Codec -> Schema -> [[ByteString]] -> IO ByteString

-- | Packs a container from a given list of already encoded Avro values
--   Each bytestring should represent exactly one one value serialised to
--   Avro.
packContainerValuesWithSync :: Codec -> Schema -> ByteString -> [[ByteString]] -> ByteString

-- | Packs a container from a given list of already encoded Avro values
--   Each bytestring should represent exactly one one value serialised to
--   Avro.
packContainerValuesWithSync' :: (Schema -> a -> Builder) -> Codec -> Schema -> ByteString -> [[a]] -> ByteString

-- | Packs a new container from a list of already encoded Avro blocks. Each
--   block is denoted as a pair of a number of objects within that block
--   and the block content.
packContainerBlocks :: Codec -> Schema -> [(Int, ByteString)] -> IO ByteString

-- | Packs a new container from a list of already encoded Avro blocks. Each
--   block is denoted as a pair of a number of objects within that block
--   and the block content.
packContainerBlocksWithSync :: Codec -> Schema -> ByteString -> [(Int, ByteString)] -> ByteString

-- | Creates an Avro container header for a given schema.
containerHeaderWithSync :: Codec -> Schema -> ByteString -> Builder
consumeN :: Int64 -> (a -> (a, b)) -> a -> (a, [b])
parseCodec :: Monad m => Maybe ByteString -> m Codec
takeWhileInclusive :: (a -> Bool) -> [a] -> [a]
instance GHC.Internal.Base.Functor Data.Avro.Internal.Container.Blocks

module Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro

-- | Descrives how to convert a given intermediate <a>Value</a> into a
--   Haskell data type.
class FromAvro a
fromAvro :: FromAvro a => Value -> Either String a

-- | An intermediate data structute for decoding between Avro bytes and
--   Haskell types.
--   
--   Because reader and writer schemas, and therefore expected data types
--   and layout can be different, deserialising bytes into Haskell types
--   directly is not possible.
--   
--   To overcome this issue this intermediate data structure is used: bytes
--   are decoded into values of type <a>Value</a> (using reader's layout
--   and rules) and then translated to target Haskell types using
--   <a>FromAvro</a> type class machinery.
data Value
Null :: Value
Boolean :: Bool -> Value
Int :: ReadSchema -> {-# UNPACK #-}Int32 -> Value
Long :: ReadSchema -> {-# UNPACK #-}Int64 -> Value
Float :: ReadSchema -> {-# UNPACK #-}Float -> Value
Double :: ReadSchema -> {-# UNPACK #-}Double -> Value
Bytes :: ReadSchema -> {-# UNPACK #-}ByteString -> Value
String :: ReadSchema -> {-# UNPACK #-}Text -> Value
Array :: Vector Value -> Value
Map :: HashMap Text Value -> Value
Record :: ReadSchema -> Vector Value -> Value
Union :: ReadSchema -> {-# UNPACK #-}Int -> Value -> Value
Fixed :: ReadSchema -> {-# UNPACK #-}ByteString -> Value
Enum :: ReadSchema -> {-# UNPACK #-}Int -> {-# UNPACK #-}Text -> Value
getValue :: ReadSchema -> Get Value

-- | Descrive the value in a way that is safe to use in error messages
--   (i.e. do not print values)
describeValue :: Value -> String
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.Value
instance Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro GHC.Types.Bool
instance Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro Data.ByteString.Lazy.Internal.ByteString
instance Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro Data.ByteString.Internal.Type.ByteString
instance Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro Data.Time.Calendar.Days.Day
instance (GHC.Internal.TypeNats.KnownNat p, GHC.Internal.TypeNats.KnownNat s) => Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro (Data.Avro.Schema.Decimal.Decimal p s)
instance Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro Data.Time.Clock.Internal.DiffTime.DiffTime
instance Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro GHC.Types.Double
instance (Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro a, Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro b) => Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro (GHC.Internal.Data.Either.Either a b)
instance Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro GHC.Types.Float
instance Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro a => Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro (Data.HashMap.Internal.HashMap Data.Text.Internal.Text a)
instance Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro a => Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro (GHC.Internal.Data.Functor.Identity.Identity a)
instance Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro GHC.Types.Int
instance Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro GHC.Internal.Int.Int32
instance Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro GHC.Internal.Int.Int64
instance Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro a => Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro [a]
instance Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro Data.Time.LocalTime.Internal.LocalTime.LocalTime
instance Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro a => Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro (Data.Map.Internal.Map Data.Text.Internal.Text a)
instance Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro a => Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro (GHC.Internal.Maybe.Maybe a)
instance Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro Data.Text.Internal.Text
instance Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro Data.Time.Clock.Internal.UTCTime.UTCTime
instance Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro Data.UUID.Types.Internal.UUID
instance Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro ()
instance (Data.Vector.Unboxed.Base.Unbox a, Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro a) => Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro (Data.Vector.Unboxed.Base.Vector a)
instance Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro a => Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.FromAvro (Data.Vector.Vector a)
instance GHC.Internal.Generics.Generic Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.Value
instance Control.DeepSeq.NFData Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.Value
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Data.Avro.Encoding.FromAvro.Value

module Data.Avro.Deriving.NormSchema

-- | Extracts all the records from the schema (flattens the schema) Named
--   types get resolved when needed to include at least one "inlined"
--   schema in each record and to make each record self-contained. Note:
--   Namespaces are not really supported in this version. All the
--   namespaces (including inlined into full names) will be ignored during
--   names resolution.
extractDerivables :: Schema -> [Schema]
getTypes :: Schema -> [(TypeName, Schema)]
normSchema :: Schema -> State (Map TypeName Schema) Schema

module Data.Avro.Deriving.Lift
instance Language.Haskell.TH.Syntax.Lift Data.Avro.Schema.Schema.Decimal
instance Language.Haskell.TH.Syntax.Lift Data.Avro.Schema.Schema.DefaultValue
instance Language.Haskell.TH.Syntax.Lift Data.Avro.Schema.Schema.Field
instance Language.Haskell.TH.Syntax.Lift Data.Avro.Schema.Schema.LogicalTypeBytes
instance Language.Haskell.TH.Syntax.Lift Data.Avro.Schema.Schema.LogicalTypeFixed
instance Language.Haskell.TH.Syntax.Lift Data.Avro.Schema.Schema.LogicalTypeInt
instance Language.Haskell.TH.Syntax.Lift Data.Avro.Schema.Schema.LogicalTypeLong
instance Language.Haskell.TH.Syntax.Lift Data.Avro.Schema.Schema.LogicalTypeString
instance Language.Haskell.TH.Syntax.Lift Data.Avro.Schema.Schema.Order
instance Language.Haskell.TH.Syntax.Lift Data.Avro.Schema.Schema.Schema
instance Language.Haskell.TH.Syntax.Lift Data.Avro.Schema.Schema.TypeName


-- | Avro encoding and decoding routines.
--   
--   This library provides a high level interface for encoding and decoding
--   Haskell values in Apache's Avro serialization format.
module Data.Avro

-- | N.B. It is possible to create a Haskell value (of <a>Schema</a> type)
--   that is not a valid Avro schema by violating one of the above or one
--   of the conditions called out in <a>validateSchema</a>.
data Schema
Null :: Schema
Boolean :: Schema
Int :: Maybe LogicalTypeInt -> Schema
[logicalTypeI] :: Schema -> Maybe LogicalTypeInt
Long :: Maybe LogicalTypeLong -> Schema
[logicalTypeL] :: Schema -> Maybe LogicalTypeLong
Float :: Schema
Double :: Schema
Bytes :: Maybe LogicalTypeBytes -> Schema
[logicalTypeB] :: Schema -> Maybe LogicalTypeBytes
String :: Maybe LogicalTypeString -> Schema
[logicalTypeS] :: Schema -> Maybe LogicalTypeString
Array :: Schema -> Schema
[item] :: Schema -> Schema
Map :: Schema -> Schema
[values] :: Schema -> Schema
NamedType :: TypeName -> Schema
Record :: TypeName -> [TypeName] -> Maybe Text -> [Field] -> Schema
[name] :: Schema -> TypeName
[aliases] :: Schema -> [TypeName]
[doc] :: Schema -> Maybe Text
[fields] :: Schema -> [Field]
Enum :: TypeName -> [TypeName] -> Maybe Text -> Vector Text -> Schema
[name] :: Schema -> TypeName
[aliases] :: Schema -> [TypeName]
[doc] :: Schema -> Maybe Text
[symbols] :: Schema -> Vector Text
Union :: Vector Schema -> Schema
[options] :: Schema -> Vector Schema
Fixed :: TypeName -> [TypeName] -> Int -> Maybe LogicalTypeFixed -> Schema
[name] :: Schema -> TypeName
[aliases] :: Schema -> [TypeName]
[size] :: Schema -> Int
[logicalTypeF] :: Schema -> Maybe LogicalTypeFixed
pattern Int' :: Schema
pattern Long' :: Schema
pattern Bytes' :: Schema
pattern String' :: Schema
data Field
Field :: Text -> [Text] -> Maybe Text -> Maybe Order -> Schema -> Maybe DefaultValue -> Field
[fldName] :: Field -> Text
[fldAliases] :: Field -> [Text]
[fldDoc] :: Field -> Maybe Text
[fldOrder] :: Field -> Maybe Order
[fldType] :: Field -> Schema
[fldDefault] :: Field -> Maybe DefaultValue
data Order
Ascending :: Order
Descending :: Order
Ignore :: Order

-- | A named type in Avro has a name and, optionally, a namespace.
--   
--   A name is a string that starts with an ASCII letter or underscore
--   followed by letters, underscores and digits:
--   
--   <pre>
--   name ::= [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*
--   </pre>
--   
--   Examples include <tt>"_foo7"</tt>, <tt><a>Bar_</a></tt> and
--   <tt>"x"</tt>.
--   
--   A namespace is a sequence of names with the same lexical structure.
--   When written as a string, the components of a namespace are separated
--   with dots (<tt>"com.example"</tt>).
--   
--   <a>TypeName</a> represents a <i>fullname</i>—a name combined with a
--   namespace. These are written and parsed as dot-separated strings. The
--   <a>TypeName</a> <tt>TN <a>Foo</a> ["com", "example"]</tt> is rendered
--   as <tt>"com.example.Foo"</tt>.
--   
--   Fullnames have to be globally unique inside an Avro schema.
--   
--   A namespace of <tt>[]</tt> or <tt>[""]</tt> is the "null namespace".
--   In avro an explicitly null-namespaced identifier is written as ".Foo"
data TypeName
TN :: Text -> [Text] -> TypeName
[baseName] :: TypeName -> Text
[namespace] :: TypeName -> [Text]

-- | The <tt>decimal</tt> logical type represents arbitrary-precision
--   decimal numbers. Numbers are represented as <tt>unscaled * (10 **
--   -scale)</tt> where <tt>scale</tt> is part of the logical type and
--   <tt>unscaled</tt> is an integer represented by the underlying
--   primitive type.
--   
--   Instances of the <tt>decimal</tt> logical type need to specify a
--   <tt>scale</tt> and <tt>precision</tt>.
--   
--   <tt>decimal</tt> can be encoded as one of several different primitive
--   types:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li><pre>bytes</pre></li>
--   <li><pre>fixed</pre></li>
--   <li><pre>long</pre></li>
--   <li><pre>int</pre></li>
--   </ul>
--   
--   For <tt>long</tt> and <tt>int</tt>, <tt>unscaled</tt> is the
--   underlying number.
--   
--   For <tt>bytes</tt> and <tt>fixed</tt>, <tt>unscaled</tt> is
--   represented as a two's-complement signed integer in big-endian byte
--   order.
--   
--   Note: <tt>int</tt> and <tt>long</tt> representations for
--   <tt>decimal</tt> are not part of the <a>current Avro
--   specification</a>, but they are supported by some language
--   implementations including the official Java library. Implementations
--   that do not support this should ignore the logical type and use the
--   underlying primitive type instead.
data Decimal
Decimal :: Integer -> Integer -> Decimal

-- | The maximum number of digits that can be represented by this
--   <tt>decimal</tt> type.
--   
--   <pre>
--   precision &gt; 0
--   </pre>
[precision] :: Decimal -> Integer

-- | The <tt>scale</tt> in <tt>unscaled * (10 ** -scale)</tt> for this
--   type.
--   
--   <pre>
--   0 ≤ scale ≤ precision
--   </pre>
[scale] :: Decimal -> Integer
newtype LogicalTypeBytes

-- | An arbitrary-precision signed decimal number. See <a>Decimal</a>.
DecimalB :: Decimal -> LogicalTypeBytes
data LogicalTypeFixed

-- | An arbitrary-precision signed decimal number. See <a>Decimal</a>.
DecimalF :: Decimal -> LogicalTypeFixed

-- | An interval of time, represented as some number of months, days and
--   milliseconds.
--   
--   Encoded as three little-endian unsigned integers for months, days and
--   milliseconds respectively.
Duration :: LogicalTypeFixed
data LogicalTypeInt

-- | An arbitrary-precision signed decimal number. See <a>Decimal</a>.
DecimalI :: Decimal -> LogicalTypeInt

-- | A date (eg <tt>2020-01-10</tt>) with no timezone/locale.
--   
--   Encoded as the number of days before/after the Unix epoch
--   (1970-01-01).
Date :: LogicalTypeInt

-- | A time of day with millisecond precision.
--   
--   Encoded as the number of milliseconds after midnight.
TimeMillis :: LogicalTypeInt
data LogicalTypeLong

-- | An arbitrary-precision signed decimal number. See <a>Decimal</a>.
DecimalL :: Decimal -> LogicalTypeLong

-- | A time of day with microsecond precision.
--   
--   Encoded as the number of microseconds after midnight.
TimeMicros :: LogicalTypeLong

-- | A UTC timestamp with millisecond precision.
--   
--   Encoded as the number of milliseconds before/after the Unix epoch
--   (1970-01-01 00:00:00.000).
TimestampMillis :: LogicalTypeLong

-- | A UTC timestamp with microsecond precision.
--   
--   Encoded as the number of microseconds before/after the Unix epoch
--   (1970-01-01 00:00:00.000000).
TimestampMicros :: LogicalTypeLong

-- | A timestamp in the local timezone, whatever that happens to be, with
--   millisecond precision.
--   
--   Encoded as the number of milliseconds before/after the Unix epoch
--   (1970-01-01 00:00:00.000).
LocalTimestampMillis :: LogicalTypeLong

-- | A timestamp in the local timezone, whatever that happens to be, with
--   microsecond precision.
--   
--   Encoded as the number of microseconds before/after the Unix epoch
--   (1970-01-01 00:00:00.000000).
LocalTimestampMicros :: LogicalTypeLong
data LogicalTypeString

-- | A Universally Unique Identifier (UUID).
--   
--   Encoded as a string that is valid according to <a>RFC 4122</a>.
UUID :: LogicalTypeString

-- | This type represents a <i>deconflicted</i> version of a
--   <tt>Schema</tt>. Schema resolution is described in Avro specification:
--   <a>https://avro.apache.org/docs/current/spec.html#Schema+Resolution</a>
--   
--   This library represents "normal" schema and "deconflicted" schema as
--   different types to avoid confusion between these two usecases (we
--   shouldn't serialise values with such schema) and to be able to
--   accomodate some extra information that links between how data is
--   supposed transformed between what reader wants and what writer has.
data ReadSchema

-- | <tt>deconflict writer reader</tt> will produce a schema that can
--   decode with the writer's schema into the form specified by the
--   reader's schema.
--   
--   Schema resolution rules are described by the specification:
--   <a>https://avro.apache.org/docs/current/spec.html#Schema+Resolution</a>
deconflict :: Schema -> Schema -> Either String ReadSchema

-- | Converts <a>Schema</a> into <a>ReadSchema</a>. This function may be
--   useful when it is known that the writer and the reader schemas are the
--   same.
readSchemaFromSchema :: Schema -> ReadSchema

-- | Serialises an individual value into Avro using the schema from its
--   coresponding <a>HasAvroSchema</a> instance.
encodeValue :: (HasAvroSchema a, ToAvro a) => a -> ByteString

-- | Serialises an individual value into Avro with the schema provided.
encodeValueWithSchema :: ToAvro a => Schema -> a -> ByteString

-- | Deserialises an individual value from Avro using the schema from its
--   coresponding <a>HasAvroSchema</a>.
--   
--   <b>NOTE</b>: <b>This function is only to be used when reader and
--   writes schemas are known to be the same.</b> Because only one schema
--   is known at this point, and it is the reader schema, <i>no
--   decondlicting</i> can be performed.
decodeValue :: (HasAvroSchema a, FromAvro a) => ByteString -> Either String a

-- | Deserialises an individual value from Avro.
decodeValueWithSchema :: FromAvro a => ReadSchema -> ByteString -> Either String a

-- | Decodes the container using a schema from <a>HasAvroSchema</a> as a
--   reader schema.
--   
--   Errors are reported as a part of the list and the list will stop at
--   first error. This means that the consumer will get all the "good"
--   content from the container until the error is detected, then this
--   error and then the list is finished.
decodeContainer :: (HasAvroSchema a, FromAvro a) => ByteString -> [Either String a]

-- | Decodes the container as a list of values of the requested type.
--   
--   Errors are reported as a part of the list and the list will stop at
--   first error. This means that the consumer will get all the "good"
--   content from the container until the error is detected, then this
--   error and then the list is finished.
decodeContainerWithEmbeddedSchema :: FromAvro a => ByteString -> [Either String a]

-- | Decodes the container as a list of values of the requested type.
--   
--   The provided reader schema will be de-conflicted with the schema
--   embedded with the container.
--   
--   Errors are reported as a part of the list and the list will stop at
--   first error. This means that the consumer will get all the "good"
--   content from the container until the error is detected, then this
--   error and then the list is finished.
decodeContainerWithReaderSchema :: FromAvro a => Schema -> ByteString -> [Either String a]

-- | Encode chunks of values into a container, using 16 random bytes for
--   the synchronization markers and a corresponding <a>HasAvroSchema</a>
--   schema. Blocks are compressed (or not) according to the given
--   <a>Codec</a> (<a>nullCodec</a> or <a>deflateCodec</a>).
encodeContainer :: (HasAvroSchema a, ToAvro a) => Codec -> [[a]] -> IO ByteString

-- | Encode chunks of values into a container, using 16 random bytes for
--   the synchronization markers. Blocks are compressed (or not) according
--   to the given <a>Codec</a> (<a>nullCodec</a> or <a>deflateCodec</a>).
encodeContainerWithSchema :: ToAvro a => Codec -> Schema -> [[a]] -> IO ByteString

-- | Encode chunks of objects into a container, using the provided
--   ByteString as the synchronization markers.
encodeContainerWithSync :: ToAvro a => Codec -> Schema -> ByteString -> [[a]] -> ByteString

-- | Generates a new synchronization marker for encoding Avro containers
newSyncBytes :: IO ByteString

-- | Splits container into a list of individual avro-encoded values.
--   
--   This is particularly useful when slicing up containers into one or
--   more smaller files. By extracting the original bytestring it is
--   possible to avoid re-encoding data.
extractContainerValuesBytes :: ByteString -> Either String (Schema, [Either String ByteString])

-- | Splits container into a list of individual avro-encoded values. This
--   version provides both encoded and decoded values.
--   
--   This is particularly useful when slicing up containers into one or
--   more smaller files. By extracting the original bytestring it is
--   possible to avoid re-encoding data.
decodeContainerValuesBytes :: FromAvro a => Schema -> ByteString -> Either String (Schema, [Either String (a, ByteString)])

-- | Describes how to encode Haskell data types into Avro bytes
class ToAvro a

-- | Descrives how to convert a given intermediate <a>Value</a> into a
--   Haskell data type.
class FromAvro a

-- | A <a>Codec</a> allows for compression/decompression of a block in an
--   Avro container according to the Avro spec.
data Codec

-- | <a>nullCodec</a> specifies <tt>null</tt> required by Avro spec. (see
--   <a>https://avro.apache.org/docs/1.8.1/spec.html#null</a>)
nullCodec :: Codec

-- | <a>deflateCodec</a> specifies <tt>deflate</tt> codec required by Avro
--   spec. (see
--   <a>https://avro.apache.org/docs/1.8.1/spec.html#deflate</a>)
deflateCodec :: Codec
class HasAvroSchema a
schema :: HasAvroSchema a => Tagged a Schema
schemaOf :: HasAvroSchema a => a -> Schema

module Data.Avro.EitherN

putIndexedValue :: ToAvro a => Int -> Vector Schema -> a -> Builder

-- | This module lets us derive Haskell types from an Avro schema that can
--   be serialized/deserialized to Avro.
module Data.Avro.Deriving

-- | Derives Avro from a given schema file. Generates data types, FromAvro
--   and ToAvro instances.
data DeriveOptions
DeriveOptions :: (Text -> Field -> Text) -> (TypeName -> Field -> (FieldStrictness, FieldUnpackedness)) -> NamespaceBehavior -> DeriveOptions

-- | How to build field names for generated data types. The first argument
--   is the type name to use as a prefix, rendered according to the
--   <a>namespaceBehavior</a> setting.
[fieldNameBuilder] :: DeriveOptions -> Text -> Field -> Text

-- | Determines field representation of generated data types
[fieldRepresentation] :: DeriveOptions -> TypeName -> Field -> (FieldStrictness, FieldUnpackedness)

-- | Controls how we handle namespaces when defining Haskell type and field
--   names.
[namespaceBehavior] :: DeriveOptions -> NamespaceBehavior

-- | Describes the strictness of a field for a derived data type. The field
--   will be derived as if it were written with a <tt>!</tt>.
data FieldStrictness
StrictField :: FieldStrictness
LazyField :: FieldStrictness

-- | Describes the representation of a field for a derived data type. The
--   field will be derived as if it were written with an <tt>{-# UNPACK
--   #-}</tt> pragma.
data FieldUnpackedness
UnpackedField :: FieldUnpackedness
NonUnpackedField :: FieldUnpackedness

-- | How to treat Avro namespaces in the generated Haskell types.
data NamespaceBehavior

-- | Namespaces are ignored completely. Haskell identifiers are generated
--   from types' base names. This produces nicer types but fails on valid
--   Avro schemas where the same base name occurs in different namespaces.
--   
--   The Avro type <tt>com.example.Foo</tt> would generate the Haskell type
--   <tt>Foo</tt>. If <tt>Foo</tt> had a field called <tt>bar</tt>, the
--   generated Haskell record would have a field called <tt>fooBar</tt>.
IgnoreNamespaces :: NamespaceBehavior

-- | Haskell types and field names are generated with namespaces. See
--   <tt>deriveAvroWithNamespaces</tt> for an example of how this works.
--   
--   The Avro type <tt>com.example.Foo</tt> would generate the Haskell type
--   <tt>Com<tt>example</tt>Foo</tt>. If <tt>Foo</tt> had a field called
--   <tt>bar</tt>, the generated Haskell record would have the field
--   <tt>com<tt>example</tt>FooBar</tt>.
HandleNamespaces :: NamespaceBehavior

-- | Provide a custom mapping from the name of the Avro type and its
--   namespace that will be used to generate Haskell types and fields.
Custom :: (Text -> [Text] -> Text) -> NamespaceBehavior

-- | Default deriving options
--   
--   <pre>
--   defaultDeriveOptions = <a>DeriveOptions</a>
--     { fieldNameBuilder  = <a>mkPrefixedFieldName</a>
--     , fieldStrictness   = <a>mkLazyField</a>
--     , namespaceBehavior = <a>IgnoreNamespaces</a>
--     }
--   </pre>
defaultDeriveOptions :: DeriveOptions

-- | Generates a field name that is prefixed with the type name.
--   
--   For example, if the schema defines type <tt>Person</tt> that has a
--   field <tt>firstName</tt>, then the generated Haskell type will be like
--   
--   <pre>
--   Person { personFirstName :: Text }
--   </pre>
mkPrefixedFieldName :: Text -> Field -> Text

-- | Generates a field name that matches the field name in schema
--   (sanitised for Haskell, so first letter is lower cased)
--   
--   For example, if the schema defines type <tt>Person</tt> that has a
--   field <tt>firstName</tt>, then the generated Haskell type will be like
--   
--   <pre>
--   Person { firstName :: Text }
--   </pre>
--   
--   You may want to enable <a>DuplicateRecordFields</a> if you want to use
--   this method.
mkAsIsFieldName :: Text -> Field -> Text

-- | Marks any field as non-strict in the generated data types.
mkLazyField :: TypeName -> Field -> (FieldStrictness, FieldUnpackedness)

-- | Make a field strict and unpacked if it has a primitive representation.
--   Primitive types are types which GHC has either a static or an unlifted
--   representation: <tt>()</tt>, <tt>Boolean</tt>, <a>Int32</a>,
--   <a>Int64</a>, <a>Float</a>, <a>Double</a>.
mkStrictPrimitiveField :: TypeName -> Field -> (FieldStrictness, FieldUnpackedness)

-- | Generates the value of type <a>Schema</a> that it can later be used
--   with <a>deriveAvro'</a> or <a>deriveAvroWithOptions'</a>.
--   
--   <pre>
--   mySchema :: Schema
--   mySchema = $(makeSchema "schemas/my-schema.avsc")
--   </pre>
makeSchema :: FilePath -> Q Exp
makeSchemaFrom :: FilePath -> Text -> Q Exp
makeSchemaFromByteString :: ByteString -> Q Exp

-- | Derives Haskell types from the given Avro schema file. These Haskell
--   types support both reading and writing to Avro.
--   
--   For an Avro schema with a top-level record called
--   <tt>com.example.Foo</tt>, this generates:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li>a <a>Schema</a> with the name <tt>schema'Foo</tt> or
--   <tt>schema<tt>com'example</tt>Foo</tt>, depending on the
--   <a>namespaceBehavior</a> setting.</li>
--   <li>Haskell types for each named type defined in the schema</li>
--   <li><tt>HasSchema</tt> instances for each type</li>
--   <li><tt>FromAvro</tt> instances for each type</li>
--   <li><a>ToAvro</a> instances for each type</li>
--   </ul>
--   
--   This function ignores namespaces when generated Haskell type and field
--   names. This will fail on valid Avro schemas which contain types with
--   the same base name in different namespaces. It will also fail for
--   schemas that contain types with base names that are the same except
--   for the capitalization of the first letter.
--   
--   The type <tt>com.example.Foo</tt> will generate a Haskell type
--   <tt>Foo</tt>. If <tt>com.example.Foo</tt> has a field named
--   <tt>Bar</tt>, the field in the Haskell record will be called
--   <tt>fooBar</tt>.
deriveAvroWithOptions :: DeriveOptions -> FilePath -> Q [Dec]

-- | Derive Haskell types from the given Avro schema.
--   
--   For an Avro schema with a top-level definition
--   <tt>com.example.Foo</tt>, this generates:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li>a <a>Schema</a> with the name <tt>schema'Foo</tt> or
--   <tt>schema<tt>com'example</tt>Foo</tt> depending on namespace
--   handling</li>
--   <li>Haskell types for each named type defined in the schema</li>
--   <li><tt>HasSchema</tt> instances for each type</li>
--   <li><tt>FromAvro</tt> instances for each type</li>
--   <li><a>ToAvro</a> instances for each type</li>
--   </ul>
deriveAvroWithOptions' :: DeriveOptions -> Schema -> Q [Dec]

-- | Same as <a>deriveAvro</a> but takes a ByteString rather than FilePath
deriveAvroFromByteString :: ByteString -> Q [Dec]

-- | Same as <a>deriveAvroWithOptions</a> but uses
--   <a>defaultDeriveOptions</a>
--   
--   <pre>
--   deriveAvro = <a>deriveAvroWithOptions</a> <a>defaultDeriveOptions</a>
--   </pre>
deriveAvro :: FilePath -> Q [Dec]

-- | Same as <a>deriveAvroWithOptions'</a> but uses
--   <a>defaultDeriveOptions</a>
--   
--   <pre>
--   deriveAvro' = <a>deriveAvroWithOptions'</a> <a>defaultDeriveOptions</a>
--   </pre>
deriveAvro' :: Schema -> Q [Dec]

-- | A quasiquoter for raw string literals - that is, string literals that
--   don't recognise the standard escape sequences (such as <tt>'\n'</tt>).
--   Basically, they make your code more readable by freeing you from the
--   responsibility to escape backslashes. They are useful when working
--   with regular expressions, DOS/Windows paths and markup languages (such
--   as XML).
--   
--   Don't forget the <tt>LANGUAGE QuasiQuotes</tt> pragma if you're using
--   this module in your code.
--   
--   Usage:
--   
--   <pre>
--   ghci&gt; :set -XQuasiQuotes
--   ghci&gt; import Text.RawString.QQ
--   ghci&gt; let s = [r|\w+@[a-zA-Z_]+?\.[a-zA-Z]{2,3}|]
--   ghci&gt; s
--   "\\w+@[a-zA-Z_]+?\\.[a-zA-Z]{2,3}"
--   ghci&gt; [r|C:\Windows\SYSTEM|] ++ [r|\user32.dll|]
--   "C:\\Windows\\SYSTEM\\user32.dll"
--   </pre>
--   
--   Multiline raw string literals are also supported:
--   
--   <pre>
--   multiline :: String
--   multiline = [r|&lt;HTML&gt;
--   &lt;HEAD&gt;
--   &lt;TITLE&gt;Auto-generated html formated source&lt;/TITLE&gt;
--   &lt;META HTTP-EQUIV="Content-Type" CONTENT="text/html; charset=windows-1252"&gt;
--   &lt;/HEAD&gt;
--   &lt;BODY LINK="#0000ff" VLINK="#800080" BGCOLOR="#ffffff"&gt;
--   &lt;P&gt; &lt;/P&gt;
--   &lt;PRE&gt;|]
--   </pre>
--   
--   Caveat: since the <tt>"|]"</tt> character sequence is used to
--   terminate the quasiquotation, you can't use it inside the raw string
--   literal. Use <a>rQ</a> if you want to embed that character sequence
--   inside the raw string.
--   
--   For more on raw strings, see e.g.
--   <a>http://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg21/docs/papers/2006/n2053.html</a>
--   
--   For more on quasiquotation, see
--   <a>http://www.haskell.org/haskellwiki/Quasiquotation</a>
r :: QuasiQuoter
instance GHC.Internal.Generics.Generic Data.Avro.Deriving.DeriveOptions
instance GHC.Internal.Generics.Generic Data.Avro.Deriving.FieldStrictness
instance GHC.Internal.Generics.Generic Data.Avro.Deriving.FieldUnpackedness
